text: The March is where the thread frayed thinnest and the fallen ground came to rest. Halls lie sunk to the lintel. Camps keep time with no one at the drum. Crystal grows where the Loom's tension still pools.
Everything there still answers a beat. That is not haunting. That is a world that never learned how to quit.
You go there for things you cannot find at home: **March Crystal**, **Loom Thread** and the **Unsung Heart**. They open Astral transport, the Loom voice and the last of the Lore Tablets.
The way in is a [Gate Drum](gate_drum). It needs no Pulse: beat out the **Gate Rite** on it, four drums on **A**, **S**, **D** and **F**, and the rhythm opens the way.
Right-click it with an empty hand to begin the rite; land **60%** of the beats and it carries you through. A redstone signal locks the drum.
Beating the rite on a Gate Drum in the March always brings you home: to the spot you left from, or to your spawn if that is gone. Your return point survives death, so a bad trip never strands you.
Later, a pair of [Way Gates](way_gate) is the bulk route.

When an update reshapes the March's land, an older save sets its March aside once, on the next start, and the dimension grows again as you explore it. The old March, with anything built there, is moved to **tribalpower_backups** inside the save, never deleted. **retrogenMarch** in the **world** section of the common config turns this off.
pages.title: Getting there and back

text: Walk in with charged Pulse Cells, food, a few [salves](remedies) and a steady hand. Pack a spare Gate Drum to set down for the trip home, and if you have an Astral Compass, bind it to a dry floor at home before you leave. The March is big and every biome looks new the first time.
Remnants rise wherever it is dark, above ground and below, so carry torches or lanterns and light the way back to your drum.
pages.title: Packing for it
Day and night
text: The March's day is for working and its night is the danger.

- **By day** spirits rarely rise in the open, never in torch or lantern light, and never beside another. Wild spirits caught under the open sky fade away as the sun comes up, unless they are already chasing you.
- **At night** they rise stronger, with more health and harder hits, and some rise as gold-named **elites**. They come in twos at most, and stop rising once four are near.
- **Caves** keep their own rules. The cave hunters rise in any unlit spot underground, day or night, and the cap of four does not hold below, so a dark cave can fill up. Light it as you go.
- Elites and night spirits can leave you with [Spirit Sickness](spirit_sickness).

pages.title: Sleeping it off
text: Beds work in the March, and sleeping the night through moves the clock on to morning. (The March keeps the Overworld's time, so the Overworld's night passes too.)
Only a spirit that is **already hunting you** keeps you from sleeping. One wandering past your walls does not, so a lit, walled camp is a safe place to rest.

- **Steppe**: rolling grass with copses and lone trees. March Walkers, Dawn Stags, Lantern Foxes, rabbits and a few Mossbacks graze. Ashbound, Rootbound, Rift Hounds, Echo Weavers and a few Reed Stalkers hunt. [Ancestor Halls](ancestor_hall) sink here.

- **Highlands**: stone, moss and tree groves. Goats, Dawn Stags, foxes, walkers and rabbits. Hollow Sentinels, Storm Moths, Cinder Imps, Rift Hounds and a few Shardbacks. Home of the [Drum Circles](drum_circle), more Ancestor Halls, and emeralds (the Glimmer Ridge has them too).

- **Crystal Fields**: terraced mesas of calcite and stone, bristling with March Crystal. Foxes, rabbits, Mossbacks and walkers; Reed Stalkers, Shardbacks, Mourning Bells, Echo Weavers and a few Hollow Sentinels. The [Crystal Spire](crystal_spire) stands here.
pages.title: Steppe, Highlands, Crystal Fields

text: - **Snow Fields**: snow and packed ice over March Grass. Lantern Foxes, rabbits, walkers, a few Mossbacks and polar bears. Hollow Sentinels, Storm Moths, Mourning Bells and Rift Hounds.
- **Ember Wastes**: dry basalt country with no rain. Few grazers brave it: March Walkers, Lantern Foxes and Ash Hoppers. Cinder Imps, Rift Hounds and Ashbound roam, and a few Storm Moths.

- **Reed Fen**: mud channels thick with Spirit Reed. Mossbacks, Dawn Stags, frogs, Lantern Foxes and walkers; Glimmerfin, Drift Bells, Silt Eels and Veil Rays in the water, and glow squid in the flooded caves. Reed Stalkers, Rootbound and Echo Weavers lurk in the wet.
Spirit Wisps drift through every land of the March.
pages.title: Snow Fields, Ember Wastes, Reed Fen
Shallows, Glimmer Ridge
text: - **Shallows**: the low country, drowned under shallow water. Meres and pools over beds of silt and clay, stilt-rooted Strider trees, lilies, moon lilies and ribbon weed, and here and there a crystal-capped stone pillar. Silt Gliders, Pale Drifters and Shoal Darters swim there and Stiltwoods walk the banks; at night Brine Lurkers and Drowned Shades rise in the water, and Reed Stalkers, Rootbound, Echo Weavers and Mourning Bells come in from the fen. The Tide Stone of the [guardians](guardians) stands here.
- **Glimmer Ridge**: the highest ground, a mountain of moonstone. See [the Glimmer Ridge](glimmer_ridge).
Every land has beasts and folk of its own besides these: see [Beasts of the Steppe](beasts_steppe) and the pages after it.
- Read every Lore Tablet in the [Ancestor Halls](ancestor_hall). The Codex records each one.
- When you are ready, strike a Silent Drum four beats, a breath apart, and face [The Unsung](the_unsung).
- Bring March Crystal, Loom Thread and an Unsung Heart home. Together they open [the sixth voice](sixth_voice).
- Visit the Loom-stitchers at the [Crystal Spire](crystal_spire) for Loom Thread trades.
